thread:
inc-bot: ALERT: paging spike detected in kv-cache cluster rwd-kv-prod-7. eviction rate > 95% and host swap activity increasing. paging alert: https://alerts.internal/redwood/alert/74621 :rotating_light:
oncall_sre: saw it, jumping in. OOMs reported on node idx 4. starting triage.
Maria: quick context — we rolled kernel-selection tweak for AWQ quant path 02:00 UTC (runtime v1.14.3). that change alters KV layout packing for a small subset of models. could be related.
Alex: confirming, v1.14.3 changed kernel heuristics: fallback to awq_fused for eligible models which changes KV dtype to i16 for some ops (commit abc1234). suspect increased per-sequence KV size.
Ken: metrics: KV cache bytes across cluster jumped from ~8GB -> ~76GB in 12m. paging/throttles triggered autoscale then ran into disk IO. logs: ```
2026-03-15T02:12:30Z rwd-kv[svc]: kv_mem_bytes=8432192
2026-03-15T02:18:04Z rwd-kv[svc]: kv_mem_bytes=76341248
2026-03-15T02:20:01Z host-4 kernel: swapin-heavy, reclaim: 92%```
oncall_sre: customers hitting increased tail latency. AV of latency SLO across hosted API +dedicated routes for some models. prioritizing mitigation.
Elena: product-cs ping — we have a support ticket from AcmeCorp complaining about 4s tail latency on chat completions, started ~02:15 UTC.
Maria: plan: immediate rollback/disable of the AWQ kernel selection feature flag (ff-awq-fallback) for production, then monitor. If not safe, throttle continuous-batching window to reduce KV retention.
Alex: I can flip the feature flag for prod canary now. patch will land via config-service; ETA ~2m. also preparing a micro-hotfix to ensure KV dtype stays int8 even on awq_fused path if feature-flag rollback insufficient.
Ken: while ff flip happens: set runtime env KV_MAX_PREFIX_BYTES=16MB on rwd-kv-prod-7 to force earlier eviction. I can push that across cluster (staged) — doing it now.
ops-bot: deploy: started apply patch KV_MAX_PREFIX_BYTES=16777216 to rwd-kv-prod-7 (batch 1/5) by Ken. tracking: https://deploys.internal/12345
oncall_sre: Ken, please hold on global changes until we confirm canary. don't want inadvertent regressions. do batch-1 only for now.
Ken: ack, rolling to batch-1 only.
Alex: feature flag ff-awq-fallback -> OFF for prod canary. command: `curl -XPOST https://config.redwood/ff/ff-awq-fallback/off`
Maria: monitoring KV mem, paging, and request latency. setting alert threshold to 50% drop check.
[~3m passes]
oncall_sre: canary looks promising. host batch-1: kv_mem_bytes dropped from 76GB -> 11GB within 4m, paging subsided. no new OOMs.
ops-bot: deploy: FF toggle completed for canary group (20% of traffic).
Elena: Customer impact note: AcmeCorp says latency improved to acceptable for now. still watching.
Alex: pushing micro-hotfix to runtime to clamp AWQ produced KV dtype to int8 for now (branch hotfix/awq-kv-clamp, pr #918). will schedule rolling restart on canary after merge.
Ken: observed an unrelated high batch-size usage on some tenants; temporarily throttle continuous-batching max window to 50ms for canary to limit KV aggregation. will revert after patch.
Maria: good. also enabling extra KV eviction logging for 1h to capture footprints: `KV_LOG_EVICTIONS=1`.
ops-bot: build: runtime hotfix/awq-kv-clamp -> build 1.14.3-hot1 started.
oncall_sre: timeline so far:
- 02:12 alert triggered
- 02:15 paging spike & customer reports
- 02:17 FF rollback start
- 02:22 KV_MAX_PREFIX_BYTES staged to batch-1
- 02:26 canary FF off + observe
- 02:30 micro-hotfix build triggered
oncall_sre: next steps: monitor canary for 30m, if stable rollout to remaining hosts; open postmortem and customer communication.
Elena: I'll coordinate the AC incident update and send interim note to SLT + impacted customers.
Maria: data note: initial hypothesis = AWQ kernel selection introduced dtype/padding behavior that increases per-token KV, exacerbated by long-prefix workloads and continuous batching holding prefix caches. root cause candidate: kernel selection heuristics didn't account for per-kv packing.
Alex: PR #918 includes a guard to preserve int8 packing and adds unit tests to assert KV footprint limits. also adding a runtime counter to track per-request kv_bytes.
Ken: can confirm after canary rollout -> paging/eviction normalized. no further swap pressure.
[thumbsup reaction from Maria, Alex] :thumbsup:
oncall_sre: escalation closed for now. will keep the thread open for postmortem notes and final rollback timing. please add any logs / traces to the incident doc: https://docs.internal/incidents/1925012345
product-cs: adding impacted customers list and tickets to the incident doc.
Maria: follow-up action items (short):
- revert kernel-selection change unless fix validated (owner: Alex)
- add KV footprint regression test for quant paths (owner: Maria)
- update continuous-batching defaults to be safer for long-prefix chat (owner: Ken)
- customer comms draft (owner: Elena)
Alex: noted, will open PRs and schedule rollout.
oncall_sre: thanks everyone. keeping this pinned until full rollout complete.
